answer: The missing property was idempotency: a rerun of the same slice must leave the target as one run would. A plain INSERT is not idempotent. After the insert committed but the success flag failed, the retry appended the same rows again and doubled the totals. Two safe designs: (1) Atomic partition replace: in one transaction, DELETE the load slice (e.g. ds = '2026-10-23') and INSERT the recomputed rows, so a retry swaps in an identical copy. (2) Version-guarded MERGE keyed on the row key, with one source row per key, so a retry matches existing rows and updates them, and an older replay cannot overwrite newer state.
